graph.summary: levodopa → aromatic-L-amino-acid decarboxylase → Dopamine → synaptic transmission, dopaminergic → Parkinson's disease

evidence.snippet: l-DOPA with the tag bonded at position 5 served as the best substrate for AADC.
evidence.explanation: Levodopa (L-DOPA) is the substrate that directly interacts with aromatic amino acid decarboxylase (AADC) at its active site; this biochemical interaction is the first step in the conversion of levodopa to dopamine.

paper.title: Enzymatic assay for perfluoro-tagged metabolites of l-DOPA using crude lysate from E. coli transformed with pKKAADCII.

evidence.snippet: recombinant human AADC, which actively catalyzes dopamine production from DOPA
evidence.explanation: AADC catalyzes the decarboxylation of L-DOPA (DOPA) to produce dopamine; this is the direct enzymatic product of AADC activity.

paper.title: Does the aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase contribute to thyronamine biosynthesis?

evidence.snippet: subsequently converted into dopamine via aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase
evidence.explanation: Review confirming that L-DOPA is converted into dopamine by the enzyme aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC).

paper.title: The role of L-DOPA in neurological and neurodegenerative complications: a review.

evidence.snippet: Dopamine's role as the principal neurotransmitter in motor functions has long been accepted.
evidence.explanation: Dopamine is the neurotransmitter that mediates dopaminergic synaptic transmission; its presence positively regulates this biological process.

paper.title: Ophthalmate is a new regulator of motor functions via CaSR: implications for movement disorders.

evidence.snippet: reduced striatal dopaminergic transmission is a transdiagnostic substrate for psychomotor retardation underlying the motor features of conditions such as Parkinson's disease
evidence.explanation: Reduced dopaminergic synaptic transmission is the defining pathophysiological feature of Parkinson's disease motor symptoms; dopaminergic transmission is therefore negatively correlated with Parkinson's disease.

paper.title: Reduced striatal dopamine transmission as a transdiagnostic substrate of psychomotor retardation.

evidence.snippet: Parkinson's Disease (PD) occurs due to extensive damage of dopamine-producing neurons; this causes dopamine deficits in the midbrain
evidence.explanation: Review confirming that dopamine deficiency (from neuronal loss) is the pathogenic basis of PD, establishing the negative correlation between dopaminergic neurotransmission and disease.

paper.title: Restoration and targeting of aberrant neurotransmitters in Parkinson's disease therapeutics.
